hypotheses.statement: The backlog stems from insufficient support staffing relative to ticket volume, not from an information/answer gap; a chatbot would only mask a capacity shortfall.

hypotheses.statement: Refund tickets pile up because the underlying refund payment processing (not the answering of questions) is slow, driving repeat/duplicate inquiries.

hypotheses.statement: Customers lack visibility into existing refund status, generating repetitive 'where is my refund' tickets that could be resolved by status notifications rather than a conversational chatbot.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because VOB-U-OVERLAP-FRACTION remains OPEN and its blocking_scope (the ticket-to-refund overlap join on DA-TCK) sits outside the actual release scope; nothing was put on hold.

Two assumptions remain unverified: A-IBAN-TICKETS-OVERLAP (that some of the 900 tickets correspond to the 5 IBAN failures, not directly measured) and A-VOLUME-IS-ABNORMAL (treating 900 tickets as abnormal with no historical baseline in evidence).

Of four proposed remedies, only two diagnostic ones (SR-OVERLAP-MEASUREMENT-JOIN, SR-TICKET-VOLUME-BASELINE) are feasible in contest time; the fix remedies (IBAN validation at submission, status notifications) are not feasible given the read-only tool_surface.
limitations_explained: VOB-U-OVERLAP-FRACTION is still OPEN: the fraction of the 900 open tickets directly caused by IBAN-failed refunds versus other causes (status inquiries, delays) was never computed; the overlap join on DA-TCK is blocked and excluded from release scope.
The IBAN-field input validation fix targeting the 5 FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records (E-01) was never built or deployed in this release.

A median response time within SLA (2.0h vs 24h, E-02) does not by itself disprove a backlog — a volume-driven symptom can persist even when per-ticket SLA is met, so the 900-ticket volume question is not fully resolved.

The tool_surface for this contest is read-only (ticket-db, payment-db), which prevented deploying the IBAN-validation-at-submission fix or proactive status notifications regardless of their diagnostic value.
Classification of the remaining non-IBAN tickets into status-inquiry/delay/other causes was not covered by the deterministic join and stays open as U-STAFFING-VS-VOLUME.

Whether 900 open tickets is actually abnormal versus steady-state volume (U-TICKET-VOLUME-BASELINE) was not tested; no historical trend data was available in the catalog, so A-VOLUME-IS-ABNORMAL remains an unverified assumption.

Of the four proposed remedies, only the two diagnostic ones (overlap measurement join, ticket-volume baseline) were feasible in contest time; overall remedy-set feasibility for actually fixing the root cause is false in this release.
proposal.summary: The support lead (SH-SUP) initially framed the problem as customers waiting too long for refund answers and requested a chatbot (CL-01/CL-02), but this hypothesis (H-RESPONSE-SPEED) was rejected: payment-db evidence (E-01) shows 5 refund records failed with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, and ticket-db evidence (E-02) shows 900 open tickets are being answered at a 2.0h median, well inside the 24h SLA. The problem definition (PD-1) therefore reframes the root problem as IBAN payment-data-quality failures combined with raw ticket volume, not a missing answer channel. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the critical unknown of what fraction of the 900 tickets are actually caused by the 5 IBAN failures (U-OVERLAP-FRACTION) as VOB-U-OVERLAP-FRACTION. What was actually released and marked DONE is two diagnostic deliverables: the packaged set of 5 FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refund records from payment-db, and the ticket-db volume/response-time baseline (900 tickets, 2.0h median vs 24h SLA). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the open VOB blocks only the ticket-to-refund overlap join, which lies outside this release's actual scope, so nothing needed to be held. No fix (IBAN validation at submission, status notifications) could be deployed because the tool surface in this contest is read-only; those, along with the overlap classification and historical baseline questions, remain explicitly open limitations.
